The six new alloys listed in Table 1 were arc-melted in Ar as button-shaped ingots (∼15 g) using pure elements: Co (99.9þ%), Ni (99.95%), Al (99.5%), Cr (99.995%), V (99.7%), Ti (99.95%), Nb (99.8%), Ta (99.95%), and B (95–97%), purchased from Alfa Aesar (Tewksbury, MA). The alloys were melted six times, with a flip between each of remelting to improve composition homogeneity.
These ingots were encapsulated in evacuated fused silica tubes, homogenized for 24 h at 1200 °C, and water quenched.
Ingot sections were aged in evacuated fused silica tubes at 850 °C for durations between 24 and 1000 h, followed by water quenching.

Figure 9 shows the microstructure of aged VTiTa: theγ 0 volume fraction of this alloy is extremely low, likely due to the precipitation of an additional phase on the grain boundaries and ubiquitously within the grains. Unlike 18Fe8Cr which precipitated Nb- and Ta-rich phases, this alloy precipitates a Ti- and Al-rich phase (as determined via EDS, shown in Figure S2, Supporting Information).
